about: The plan a driver makes for a deploy (or, with roll_back, for rolling back to an earlier one): the text an owner reads before they approve, and its SHA-256, hex, which is the deploy's plan and so in the operation they sign. The daemon (a box recomputes it before it applies) and the server must make it byte for byte the same. It starts arugula deploy plan v1, the driver, the environment's name and the source; apps-platform adds what it pins where; then a line per setting (sorted by name), the roll back and what it goes back to, and what the driver does, in words: chant-fly always, arugula-release unless it's a roll back (it never rolls back), planter's unless it's a roll back of one other than Go live. A source a driver can't deploy is planned with its refusal in the text. Settings here are as settings fills them (drivers/settings).

cases.about: arugula-release: a patch release of the daemon

output.text:
arugula deploy plan v1
driver arugula-release
environment release
source commit 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
where arugula-salad/arugula
setting bump patch
setting lane daemon
does: check commit 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 is on arugula-salad/arugula's main and passed CI (its ci/green tag, and no ci/revoked one), on a box made for this deploy, or stop
does: run scripts/release bump patch 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567, as that commit has it (what just release runs): a patch bump of the daemon's version (every arugula crate but the app), from the higher of the commit's version and main's; the run's log and the deploy's name the script's blob id
does: stop if main has no docs/releases/X.Y.Z.md for the new version, the tag is there already, or the commit is in a release already
does: commit the bump on top of the commit, tag it vX.Y.Z, and push the tag and main (the bump merged into it) in one atomic push over https
does: follow the tag's release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml) for at most 45 minutes; the release is out once its publish job succeeded. Its own secrets (the updater key, Apple's, the marketplaces') stay in GitHub Actions
with: an installation token of the platform's GitHub App that writes arugula-salad/arugula's contents and nothing else, minted for this run, and revoked right after the push; and one that only reads its Actions runs and contents, to follow the workflow, revoked when that ends
check: before either token is minted, the platform checks with GitHub that commit 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 is on main and passed CI
no roll back: a release is never taken back; a bad release is fixed by a new patch release, deployed the same way
